{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-17, in his words: "pruning amount of tools. I think I saw we have 180+ tools now. One thing I learned on storyflow project on dimensions of an entity is that each dimension needs to be orthogonal to the rest (dot product is near 0 to the rest of the dimensional vectors). While we are talking about tools versus dimensions, I feel there is some similarities. If any tool is not orthogonal/unique to the rest, it leaves the agent debating which of 2 or more tools it should use, which also leads to cases where results are inconsistent based on whether you used tool_A or tool_B, which were too close in function that the agent couldn't determine which of the two tools to use. Pruning also allows us to get down to an essential set of tools, which eases the amount" [of context every session pays].

═══ THE FAILURE HE NAMES, WITNESSED THIS SAME DAY ═══
Not hypothetical. In one session on 2026-09-17 the agent building reflow2 itself: called record_change when it meant add_change_event (one is the epoch-snapshot form, the other the design-change record — the refusal explained the difference after the fact); confused set_artifact_checksum with set_artifact_checksums; hit the contain_component / move_component pair the design already records as the discoverable sequence that CAUSES the multiple_parents defect. Each is exactly "tool_A or tool_B, too close to tell, different results".

═══ MEASURED BEFORE RECORDING, 2026-09-17 ═══
· 184 toolsnaps on disk, 186 served after #529. By verb: set_* 21, add_* 20, reconcile_* 4, release_* 4, create_* 4, acknowledge_* 3, get_* 3, record_* 3.
· Five singular/plural pairs by name alone: acknowledge_gap(s), create_edge(s), create_node(s), dimension_drift(s), set_artifact_checksum(s); plus gap_to_prompt / gaps_to_prompts and release_includes / release_includes_all.
· A DOT PRODUCT OVER DESCRIPTIONS (bag of words, tf-idf, cosine, run on the toolsnaps): 10 pairs at cosine >= 0.5. The closest: add_interface ~ add_project 0.87, add_epoch ~ plan_epoch 0.78, acknowledge_defect ~ acknowledge_gap 0.64, propagate_change ~ propagate_from 0.62, acknowledge_gaps ~ set_artifact_checksums 0.57, create_edges ~ create_nodes 0.54.
· ⚠️ AND THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN LESSON: the top pair (add_interface ~ add_project) shares almost no FUNCTION — it shares the boilerplate sentence every constructor carries ("calling again with an existing id REVISES"); the bulk tools cluster on "all or nothing". A dot product over the words of descriptions measures shared prose, not shared job. The dimension analogy holds for the JOB vector, and the job is what the find_tools corpus already encodes: one query per tool in a user's words.

═══ WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS ═══
· dec:a-tool-carries-the-users-phrasing-and-the-corpus-is-the-test (accepted): every tool must reach find_tools' top 5 for its own query; two are exempt at rank 6 with the measured reason. That test is HALF an orthogonality check — it says each tool is findable, not that two tools are distinguishable.
· fact:find-tools-misses-split… (2026-09-11): 41 of 53 misses were tools crowded out by neighbours with shared words — closeness, measured, from the other side.
· dec:bl-155 (open): 40 of 132 tools never called in a retained sample, and reflow2 cannot tell "unused" from "unreachable"; usage_report now keeps a ledger per project.
· dec:the-tool-surface-slices-hold-no-function-of-their-own: the twelve slices are surface, so a prune moves nothing in the engine.
· The typed-helper rule (the_commonest_edge_has_a_typed_helper): satisfies, constrains, allocate … exist beside create_edge ON PURPOSE, each carrying a guard or a computation the generic call lacks. That is the criterion a prune must respect: a tool earns its place by DOING something no other tool does; a second name for the same behaviour is the thing to remove.
· Every served tool's schema is loaded by every MCP client on every session (Grok Build hides them behind a search precisely because of this); the context cost he names is real and per-session.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
A. ⭐ MEASURE CONFUSABILITY FROM THE CORPUS, NOT THE PROSE: for each tool's query, which OTHER tools land in the top 5 — a confusability graph (the scorer and the corpus exist; this is a few lines over them). Join it with the usage ledger (dec:bl-155's instrument, per project) and hand the person a ranked list of pairs: "these two answer the same question and one is never called". The prune list becomes a finding, never taste. Cheapest first step; decides nothing by itself.
B. FOLD THE SINGULAR/PLURAL PAIRS: one tool taking one-or-many (the bulk forms are already all-or-nothing) — up to seven tools gone, and the record_change / add_change_event kind of confusion is not among them. ⚠️ Counter: the bulk forms carry the item-numbered refusal ("[6] CONTAINS … not found"), which the singular reply never needed; folding must keep it.
C. THE EARNS-ITS-PLACE RULE AS A GATE: a served tool must do something no other tool does (a guard, a computation, a read shape); a tool that only renames another is refused at the surface the way an undescribed tool is today. Turns pruning from a one-off into a discipline; ⚠️ it needs A's instrument to be checkable rather than argued.
D. A DEFAULT SURFACE AND AN ON-DEMAND REST: serve the core (the tools most sessions call) by default and the rest through find_tools / a profile (tools/agent_surface_profile.py already exists; the latent surface already grows itself). Cuts the per-session cost without deleting anything. ⚠️ Counter: a tool nobody sees is a tool nobody calls — the unreachable half of dec:bl-155 gets worse by construction, and the three-legs rule says the detector and the instruction still have to point at it.
E. NOTHING: the corpus test is the check, and 2 of 186 are exempt. ⚠️ Counter, his and this session's: the failure is not findability, it is two findable tools for one job, and today's session produced three instances of it.

═══ THE HONEST LIMIT ═══
Dimensions of an entity are measures and can be made independent; tools are verbs on one shared graph, and some overlap is composition — a report reading what a write wrote — not redundancy. Orthogonality is the right test for PAIRS THAT ANSWER THE SAME QUESTION, and the corpus is where that question is written down; it is the wrong test for a read and the write it reads.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — 186 served tools: should the surface be pruned to an essential set on an orthogonality test (no two tools close enough that an agent debates which to call and gets different results from each), and what instrument measures closeness — description words, the corpus, or usage?","rationale":"Captured under the brainstorm skill from Anthony's question, nothing promoted. Measured before recording because the analogy suggested an instrument (a dot product) that could be run in a minute, and running it showed the instrument measures the wrong thing — shared prose, not shared job — which is the most useful finding in the record: the corpus, not the descriptions, is where a tool's job vector lives. Recorded separately from dec:bl-155 because that one is about tools nobody calls and this one is about tools nobody can tell apart; a prune needs both.","status":"proposed"}
